juicy_reason: One-line fix prevents silent data corruption by adding a shallow copy before in-place mutations—classic Python gotcha that breaks caller expectations.
Batching logic ignored OpenAI's 300k token limit, sending 673k tokens and exploding with 400 errors on large document sets—math fail meets API reality.
Retry decorator was commented out, so `max_retries` parameter silently did nothing—users thought they had resilience but got instant failures.
Multi-turn reasoning agents silently lost their chain-of-thought because serialization forgot to write `reasoning_content` back to `thinking`.
Conversation summarization orphaned tool responses from their AI message parents, breaking the call-response chain agents rely on.
Callback manager merge was cross-contaminating handler lists because add_handler() polluted both buckets when inherit=True—classic list-mixing footgun.
Named colors like 'white' got prefixed with '!' but never URL-encoded, causing mermaid.ink API to 400—classic forgot-to-escape bug.
Mermaid diagram generation was completely broken because '!' in '!white' wasn't URL-encoded, causing 400 errors from the API.
Default parameter values from Pydantic schemas were ignored, forcing callers to manually pass defaults every time.
Modern LLM providers switched from `function_call` to `tool_calls` and the code was still checking the deprecated field, silently losing tool invocation data.
